\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അടുത്തിടെ} (aṭuttiṭe)}{അടുത്തിടെ (aṭuttiṭe)}]{\ml{അടുത്തിടെ} (aṭuttiṭe) — recently}

\label{lesson:ML-C178-atuttite}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for anyone, then the Malayalam for anything.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അടുത്തിടെ}}
\textbf{\ml{അടുത്തിടെ}} — \emph{aṭuttiṭe} — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}. Malayalam's past does not change for \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}you\textquotedblright{} or \textquotedblleft{}he\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{അടുത്തിടെ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{പുസ്തകം} \ml{വായിച്ചു}} — \emph{ñān aṭuttiṭe oru pustakaṁ vāyiccu} — \textquotedblleft{}I recently read a book.\textquotedblright{}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭuttiṭe}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for anyone, then the Malayalam for anything, then say \emph{aṭuttiṭe} again
